icps.label: Insured US adult who needs a new in-network clinician and keeps hitting inaccurate directories and unanswered phones

context.coverage: commercial, marketplace, or Medicare Advantage plan with a network
context.situation: new plan, new city, new specialty need, or a departing provider
context.channel_state: starts at an insurer directory or a general web/AI search

triggers.text: Insurer directory lists in-network clinicians who are unreachable, not accepting new patients, or out of network in practice
Hours spent calling clinics with no callback
Needs to confirm coverage before the visit to avoid a surprise bill

roles.label: provider office front desk / insurer network rules

constraints: must be in-network for a specific named plan variant
disqualifiers: uninsured or cash-pay only (no supporting evidence in this manifest)
open_questions: What share of these searches begin in an AI assistant rather than an insurer portal? No evidence found.
Which specialties dominate the unmet-access problem outside mental health?

icps.label: US patient with an acute, near-term need choosing a care setting and a bookable slot in the next 24-72 hours

context.situation: acute symptom with no near-term opening at their own clinician
context.alternatives_considered: urgent care, walk-in clinic, video visit, waiting

triggers.text: Own clinician has no near-term opening; patient asks where to go today
Category is organized around same-day and 24-72 hour availability

constraints: cost exposure unknown at decision time
must still be in-network to avoid a bill
disqualifiers: emergency-severity symptoms, which belong to emergency care and are out of this panel's scope
open_questions: How often does this need resolve at a walk-in clinic without any online search? Not measurable from public evidence.

icps.label: Caregiver booking care for a dependent (child or aging parent), most acutely for pediatric behavioral health

context.situation: seeking in-network care for someone else, with school/work scheduling constraints

triggers.text: Parent contacted dozens of listed child providers; 39 of 50 were unreachable or would not schedule, and he eventually used an out-of-network provider

open_questions: Is the aging-parent/Medicare caregiver variant distinct enough to need its own jobs? Only one weak source touches Medicare members (source-006).

icps.label: Owner or office manager of an independent US medical or dental practice evaluating or already paying for per-booking new-patient acquisition

context.geography: United States, concentrated in dense metros
context.situation: unfilled schedule slots and unclear cost per acquired patient
context.current_spend: pay-per-booking marketplace fees, paid search, or fixed-fee scheduling software

triggers.text: Charged repeatedly for patients the practice could not actually see
Per-booking fee increased sharply year over year
Marketplace-sourced patients showed a much higher no-show rate and roughly 6% one-year repeat rate
Fees are not visible until late in sign-up and vary by specialty and region

roles.label: compliance concern about paying per federal-program patient

constraints: fee must stay below realistic new-patient value
must not create Anti-Kickback Statute exposure when treating Medicare/Medicaid patients
needs spend caps and the ability to pause
disqualifiers: large health systems with their own scheduling stack (no buyer-language evidence in this manifest)
open_questions: Are dental practices a materially different buyer from primary care given the reported fee spread? Evidence suggests yes but only from a competitor-published source (source-009).

icps.label: Practice front-desk / operations lead losing appointment calls to hold time and voicemail

triggers.text: Patients report that offices do not pick up or call back

open_questions: The relevant product announcement page was not retrievable (HTTP 403). No practice-side language about phone bottlenecks was found; the trigger is inferred from the patient side.

icps.label: Health-plan digital experience owner embedding in-network booking into a member portal

context.situation: members rely on plan directories that do not produce appointments

triggers.text: A regional plan embedded third-party booking into its member portal with a 90-day booking window

constraints: network integrity and directory accuracy obligations
open_questions: No payer-side buyer language, RFP, or procurement evidence was found. One deal is not a segment.

standing_claims.text: The target operates a US patient-facing marketplace to find and book in-person or telemedicine appointments, filtered by insurance, location, specialty, and availability
The target performs insurance plan matching and, for supported carriers, active-coverage checks, but states this does not guarantee in-network coverage
The target states appointments are typically scheduled within 24-72 hours
Providers pay a one-time booking fee when a new patient books; there is no upfront or subscription cost; the fee varies by specialty and location and is charged at booking, not on visit outcome

Third-party sources report per-new-patient fees in a roughly $35-$110 range varying by specialty and region; the publisher of that figure sells a competing product and the target does not publish a fee schedule

HHS-OIG advisory opinions (2019, 2023) concluded the per-booking fee model implicated but did not violate the Anti-Kickback Statute, and the Second Circuit affirmed dismissal of a whistleblower challenge in 2025
An AI phone assistant product for practices is claimed in the perimeter but its announcement page was not retrievable and no independent source was obtained
A regional health plan embedded the target's booking into its member portal (June 2025)

counterevidence.text: The target's own page states insurance verification does not guarantee in-network coverage, which directly qualifies the marketplace's core promise
Provider complainants describe fees for bookings that could not be honored, sharp fee increases, and a review-policy dispute
A first-person practice account reports higher no-shows and a 6% one-year repeat rate, and discontinued use
A major software review directory carries zero reviews for the product, so no aggregated provider-satisfaction corpus exists there

open_research_questions: No first-party customer corpus, site-search log, or AI-conversation log was supplied; every buyer-language source here is a public proxy.
Target root domain, /about/, /languages, and /about/news/ returned HTTP 403, so first-party positioning language is under-sampled and the slogan/flattering-claim lexicon may be incomplete.
No evidence exists for prompt prevalence in any AI surface, so exposure weighting cannot be sourced.
Spanish-language demand is asserted only by an indexed page title; no Spanish buyer behavior was found.
